texts.li: {A_nameDef} spent the morning tugging at {A_possessive} badly made {THING}, which never sat right.
The stitching on {A_nameDef}'s {THING} gave way again, in a new place this time.
{A_nameDef} held {A_possessive} {THING} up to the light and counted the thin patches.
By midday {A_nameDef}'s badly made {THING} had rubbed a sore spot raw.
{A_nameDef} sat up after supper patching {A_possessive} {THING} again.
[winter|cold] The wind found every gap in {A_nameDef}'s badly sewn {THING}.
[rain] The rain came through {A_nameDef}'s {THING} at every seam.
[working] {A_nameDef} had to stop work twice to fix {A_possessive} {THING}.
[child] {A_nameDef} tore {A_possessive} badly made {THING} again and came to ask for a needle.
{A_nameDef} stepped over the {THING} lying in the way for the fourth time today.
{A_nameDef} tripped over the {THING} that should have been put away by now.
{A_nameDef} nearly went down on {A_possessive} face over the {THING} left lying about.
{A_nameDef} has started taking the long way round the {THING} still lying in the same spot.
{A_nameDef} asked whose job it was to haul the {THING}, and didn't get an answer.
{A_nameDef} lost part of the morning working around the {THING} and everything else left lying about.
{A_nameDef} wanted to know who had left the {THING} lying about, and said so loudly.
Grime in every corner of the {THING}, and {A_nameDef} had to be in there anyway.
{A_nameDef} tried not to touch anything in the {THING}.
"Who let the {THING} get like this?" {A_nameDef} asked.
{A_nameDef}'s boots came out of the {THING} dirtier than they went in.
The dirt in the {THING} had come in on every pair of boots in the colony, and {A_nameDef} said so.
[summer|hot] The {THING} smelled of old dirt in the heat, and {A_nameDef} breathed through {A_possessive} mouth.
{A_nameDef} woke on the {THING} with one arm numb to the elbow.
{A_nameDef} turned over on the {THING} all night and got up more tired than {A_pronoun} went down.
[winter|cold] The cold came straight up through the {THING}, and {A_nameDef} was up before dawn to get warm.
[old] {A_nameDef}'s back made itself heard all morning after another night on the {THING}.
[rain] {A_nameDef} got to the table soaked through from the long walk over.
{A_nameDef} set off for supper early, to get there before it went cold.
[morning] Half awake, {A_nameDef} made the long walk to breakfast and nearly fell asleep at the table.
{A_nameDef} has been sharing {A_possessive} room with the {THING} for days now.
[night] {A_nameDef} walked into the {THING} in the dark on the way to bed.
{A_nameDef} has asked twice for the {THING} to be taken out of {A_possessive} room.
{A_nameDef} came in from the rain with {A_possessive} teeth chattering and nothing dry to change into.
{A_nameDef} worked bent over against the rain, water running off the end of {A_possessive} nose.
By the end of the job {A_nameDef}'s clothes were soaked through and twice as heavy.
